title: Ronald Reagan and Mikhail Gorbachev: 'Tear Down This Wall!' (1987)
summary: On June 12, 1987, speaking at the Brandenburg Gate in West Berlin, President Ronald Reagan issued his immortal challenge to Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev: 'Tear down this wall!'
keywords: Ronald Reagan and Gorbachev: 'Tear Down This Wall!'
full_text:
On June 12, 1987, standing before the neoclassical columns of the Brandenburg Gate in West Berlin, United States President Ronald Reagan addressed a crowd of forty-five thousand people, his words carried by loudspeakers into communist East Berlin.

Behind him stood the stark concrete barrier of the Berlin Wall, topped with barbed wire and watchtowers, which had divided families and symbolized the Cold War division of Europe since 1961.

Addressing Soviet General Secretary Mikhail Gorbachev, who was introducing political reforms (Glasnost) in Moscow, Reagan delivered one of the most powerful rhetorical climaxes of the twentieth century:

"General Secretary Gorbachev, if you seek peace, if you seek prosperity for the Soviet Union and Southern and Eastern Europe, if you seek liberalization: Come here to this gate!
Mr. Gorbachev, open this gate!
Mr. Gorbachev... tear down this wall!"

Twenty-nine months later, on November 9, 1989, peaceful crowds of joyful citizens dismantled the Berlin Wall with sledgehammers, bringing a peaceful end to the Cold War and reuniting Europe in freedom.

moral: Artificial barriers cannot withstand humanity's innate longing for freedom; courage and open diplomacy conquer division.
moral_reflection: Freedom cannot be contained by concrete walls; open the gates to human liberty.
